nodes.description: Severe influenza A pneumonitis progressing to ARDS in a subset of patients, representing a less common clinical presentation than childhood herpes simplex encephalitis.

evidence.reference_title: Severe influenza pneumonitis in children with inherited TLR3 deficiency.
evidence.snippet: three unrelated children with influenza A virus (IAV) infection manifesting as acute respiratory distress syndrome (IAV-ARDS)

nodes.description: Intravenous acyclovir is the standard treatment for HSV-1 encephalitis and is started empirically on clinical suspicion; it treats the infectious episode but does not correct the underlying interferon defect.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic defects of brain immunity in childhood herpes simplex encephalitis.
evidence.snippet: HSE is a devastating condition in all age groups, proving fatal in more than 70% of patients in the absence of treatment, and with mild-to-severe neurological sequelae in about 40–60% of acyclovir-treated survivors15,16

nodes.description: Impaired TLR3 signaling reduces cell-intrinsic induction of IFN-beta and IFN-lambda in non-hematopoietic cells (fibroblasts, cortical neurons, pulmonary epithelial cells), while circulating leukocytes retain TLR3-independent interferon responses.
nodes.id: Deficient Type I and III Interferon Induction

evidence.reference_title: Severe influenza pneumonitis in children with inherited TLR3 deficiency.
evidence.snippet: TLR3-mutated fibroblasts produce lower levels of IFN-β and -λ, and display enhanced viral susceptibility

evidence.reference_title: Genetic defects of brain immunity in childhood herpes simplex encephalitis.
evidence.snippet: Investigations of IEIs underlying HSE and other viral diseases progressively led to recognition that the TLR3-type I IFN circuit may govern the first line of broad antiviral responses in some cell types (e.g. cortical neurons and pulmonary epithelial cells) and in some specific tissues and organs (e.g. the brain and the lung)

nodes.description: Childhood HSV-1 encephalitis, the hallmark and often sole severe infectious episode.

evidence.reference_title: TLR3 deficiency in patients with herpes simplex encephalitis.
evidence.snippet: We report a dominant-negative TLR3 allele in otherwise healthy children with herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) encephalitis.

nodes.description: In the central nervous system, TLR3 is required for cortical-neuron-intrinsic type I interferon immunity to HSV-1; its loss leaves neurons unable to control viral replication.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic defects of brain immunity in childhood herpes simplex encephalitis.
evidence.snippet: The available data from hPSC-based experiments clearly indicate that TLR3-dependent, IFN-α/β-mediated cortical neuron- and oligodendrocyte-autonomous anti-HSV-1 immunity, as opposed to the innate and adaptive immunity mediated by leukocytes and related cells, is crucial for host defense against HSV-1 in the human forebrain.

nodes.description: In the lung, defective TLR3-dependent interferon responses in pulmonary epithelial cells permit uncontrolled influenza A replication, underlying severe pneumonitis and ARDS in a subset of patients.

evidence.reference_title: Severe influenza pneumonitis in children with inherited TLR3 deficiency.
evidence.snippet: the patients' iPSC-derived pulmonary epithelial cells (PECs) are susceptible to IAV. Treatment with IFN-α2b or IFN-λ1 rescues this phenotype.

nodes.description: Type I (IFN-alpha2b) and type III (IFN-lambda1) interferon rescue the cell-intrinsic antiviral defect in patient-derived cells in vitro, providing mechanistic rationale for interferon-based approaches; clinical use is not established.

evidence.reference_title: Severe influenza pneumonitis in children with inherited TLR3 deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Treatment with IFN-α2b or IFN-λ1 rescues this phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic defects of brain immunity in childhood herpes simplex encephalitis.
evidence.snippet: treatment with commercially available IFN-α2 or IFN-β, in addition to acyclovir, might be beneficial in HSE patients whose cells respond to IFN-α/β

evidence.reference_title: Severe influenza pneumonitis in children with inherited TLR3 deficiency.
evidence.snippet: three unrelated children with influenza A virus (IAV) infection manifesting as acute respiratory distress syndrome (IAV-ARDS), heterozygous for rare TLR3 variants (P554S in two patients and P680L in the third) causing autosomal dominant (AD) TLR3 deficiency

nodes.description: Germline TLR3 variants abolish (recessive complete) or partially impair (dominant-negative) TLR3-mediated signaling in response to double-stranded RNA, the initiating molecular lesion. TLR3-mutated fibroblasts do not respond to the synthetic dsRNA analog poly(I:C).

evidence.reference_title: Herpes simplex virus encephalitis in a patient with complete TLR3 deficiency: TLR3 is otherwise redundant in protective immunity.
evidence.snippet: resulting in an absence of response to TLR3 activation by polyinosinic-polycytidylic acid (poly(I:C)) and related agonists in his fibroblasts
